summary: The core OWNER_ENGINE-to-TASK_GATEWAY wiring (gateway.py's new --mode owner-dispatch / route_and_dispatch / dispatch_to_task_lifecycle, the shared REQUIRED_TASK_SECTIONS dedup, and the classifier TASK_ID entity) is clean, additive, uses subprocess argv lists (no shell injection), and is genuinely covered by passing tests (verified: 5/5 pass locally). However, this diff also rewrites PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml to make --mode owner-dispatch the 'preferred' real entrypoint for every raw Owner message going forward, and the actual dispatch code has real safety gaps that the runbook text glosses over: it completely skips the mandatory clarification gate (query.py's needs_owner_clarification, per OWNER_ENGINE_MANDATORY_GATE_IMPLEMENTATION_2026-07-25.yaml) before auto-issuing a real task-gateway.py start; it fires 'start' immediately after 'submit' even when submit's own duplicate_found signal says the task already exists, contradicting the standing NO DUPLICATION/NO COLLISION rule; and the repo auto-selection for 'start' silently defaults to claude-control with no real override checkpoint despite the code comment claiming one exists. A secondary claimed fix (credit-accountant.py propose call added to cmd_start) passes an untested --repo flag that credit-accountant.py's only other real call site (preflight-guard.py) never uses, so it may error out and silently no-op every time, meaning the claimed gap fix is unverified and possibly non-functional. None of this is destructive or touches .github/workflows, migrations, auth, or payment paths, but because this PR reclassifies the recommended operational path for real Owner-triggered task creation, these gaps should be closed (add the clarification check, gate 'start' on duplicate_found, verify the credit-accountant CLI contract) before this becomes the standard entrypoint.
issues: route_and_dispatch()/dispatch_to_task_lifecycle() in scripts/prompt_gateway/gateway.py never checks needs_owner_clarification (computed only by scripts/prompt_gateway/query.py, a separate script this new code never calls) before auto-issuing a real task-gateway.py submit/start/status call -- the PROTOCOL_OWNER_AI.yaml S1_GATED state machine documents branch_A (clarification) as gating branch_C (auto-dispatch), but the real code dispatches immediately with no such check, so an ambiguous/low-confidence Owner message can trigger a real systemd unit start and credit spend that should have been routed to S1a_CLARIFY instead.

In dispatch_to_task_lifecycle()'s action=='start' branch (scripts/prompt_gateway/gateway.py), 'start' is invoked immediately after 'submit' regardless of submit's own duplicate_found result -- it only checks whether instruction_id is present, not whether the task is a known duplicate -- bypassing the NO DUPLICATION/NO COLLISION principle (SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md step 8/9) for a fully automated code path that creates a real task and starts a real systemd worker unit.

_derive_repo_from_spec() silently falls back to DEFAULT_REPO ('claude-control') when no KNOWN_REPOS name is literally present in the spec text, and the inline comment claims 'a caller can override before anything downstream of start runs' -- but dispatch_to_task_lifecycle() actually calls the real task-gateway.py start command synchronously in the same call, before any caller sees derived_repo, so a full-spec Owner message that doesn't name its target repo gets a real task dispatched to a possibly-wrong repo with no real override opportunity.

task-gateway.py's cmd_start now calls credit-accountant.py propose with a --repo argument that the only other existing call site (scripts/preflight-guard.py's check_credit_accountant_approval) never passes; credit-accountant.py itself is not in this repo (operational-only, deployed separately per ai-os/MASTER_INDEX.yaml) so the --repo flag's existence could not be verified in review -- if unsupported, argparse will reject the call, propose_result silently falls into the 'did not return parseable JSON' branch (non-fatal, swallowed), and the specific gap this task claims to fix (worker-entrypoint.sh's later 'report --increment 1' failing with 'no matching approved plan') would remain unfixed despite the commit message stating it is fixed.
